### Round two: errors, edges, tests, and documentation

The setting will use the existing resolver’s default and validation behavior. Invalid values fall back to the existing default; the report view will not introduce a separate fallback policy or view-local settings object. This keeps defaults and resolution owned by `settings/resolver.ts:12`, with `ui/report-view.ts:30` consuming the resolved value through the already-traced settings path.

The setting remains in memory. This change adds no persistence mechanism and makes no public API or configuration-shape changes. Keeping filters across workspace changes is a separate, explicit requirement: switching workspaces must not reset their current values. That requirement does not imply preserving them after the application’s in-memory state is discarded.

Verification will exercise both the resolver boundary and the report-view behavior. Resolver coverage checks the default and invalid-input cases; report-view coverage checks that the resolved value actually controls the view and that a workspace switch retains current filters. Tests should extend the existing suites for those owners rather than introduce a parallel settings harness. The names below describe proposed test cases, not tests already run.

## Tests
- An unset report-view setting resolves to the existing default — resolver test: “uses the existing report-view default.”
- A valid report-view setting reaches the view through the shared resolver — report-view test: “uses the resolved report-view setting.”
- An invalid value falls back to the existing default — resolver test: “falls back for an invalid report-view setting.”
- Current report filters remain unchanged across workspace switches — report-view test: “retains filters when the workspace changes.”
- The change introduces neither persistent storage nor a public API/configuration-shape change — diff review of the resolver and report-view changes.

## Documentation impact
- Feature / user-facing docs introduced: none
- Materially amended existing docs: none
- Derived / memory docs invalidated: none

Applying `reference/documentation-impact.md`, no product-facing documentation change is warranted: this is a private setting using an existing ownership boundary, and no existing guide covers the view. The gathered draft’s `Docs touched: none` remains appropriate.

Do you approve round two?
